findings.where: Hero, first screen at both widths: the pad-yellow behind Mark's line 'In my view, we are at a turning point…'
findings.fault: The yellow is set as a separate strip behind each line. Every strip ends at a different width, and thin ivory gaps show between them. It looks like someone has gone over the sentence with a highlighter pen. It doesn't look like the brief's quiet 'colour memory' of a legal pad behind one quotation or panel. Because the strip hugs each line, Mark's own heading looks marked up by a reader, not set by its author.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for 'refined, never childish', with the yellow kept to a colour memory behind one quotation or panel. Mark too: a development-bank visitor's first look at him is a sentence that seems to have been marked up with a student's highlighter, which works against the legal journal's gravitas this direction is meant to have.

findings.where: Article specimen: the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' at both widths, and the closing paragraph's 'the world's best PPP law'
findings.fault: These use straight typewriter apostrophes. The same article uses curly quotation marks everywhere else: 'chapter topics', “What is the best…”, ‘Abundance’. The straight mark is most visible in the large serif title, where it looks like an unset keyboard character.
findings.who_objects: A reader used to legal and policy journals, where straight quotes in a title look like a draft, not a finished page. Angélique will also copy the specimen when she adds articles, so the mix would carry over.

findings.where: Photo captions: the hero portrait's 'Placeholder…' caption (right-aligned outside the frame at 1440, centred inside the frame at 390) and the article image's caption 'Mark Moseley at the lectern…' (left-aligned)
findings.fault: The same part, a small sans caption under a photograph, takes three different alignments on one page: right, centred and left. On the phone the centred hero caption also sits apart from the left-aligned line and paragraph below it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether this look holds when Angélique adds images and captions (a binding point in the brief). The caption treatment the tile shows is not one rule but three.

findings.where: Motion specimen at both widths: the replayed line 'In my view, we are at a turning point…' beside the curve
findings.fault: The line the motion sketch replays is set plain on the paper, without the pad-yellow behind it that the hero line has. The sketch is meant to show the hero's entrance, but the element it animates is not treated like the hero element. The founder can't see how the yellow strips behave as the line rises and fades in.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the motion sketch as the record of how the first screen enters. Here it shows a different-looking line from the one a visitor sees.
